provider: Docker Hub (free Personal plan, public repositories)

free_tier.stated: Unlimited public repositories on the free Personal plan; NO documented storage cap on public repositories. Docker's own limits table lists only pull-rate and repository counts, with no storage row. Docker's Feb 2025 policy post says storage-based billing is 'indefinitely delayed' with a promised six-month notice.

retention.stated: Pull count 100/6h anonymous or 200/6h authenticated per IP — that is the binding constraint for a 500GB-1TiB/day fetch workload (needs few, large blobs rather than many small ones)

egress.terms: Free and unmetered per-GB; the gate is a pull COUNT, not bytes: 'Unauthenticated users: 100 per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 subnet' and 'Personal (authenticated): 200' per 6 hours. Blobs are served by 307 redirect to a CDN, so one pull can be a multi-GB blob.

tooling: oras push / docker push; purpose-built wrapper: github.com/Androsh7/layerstash (chunks >5GB files into ~5GB layers, uploads to Docker Hub or GHCR; author reports 1.8TB personally stored), github.com/xausky/DockerRegisterCloud (654 stars, registry-as-netdisk client with Flutter GUI + direct-download server).
chaining: Unlimited public repos per account, and the free account count itself is unlimited. Layer count per repo is not capped, so a single repo holds arbitrarily many blobs; layerstash's <base-tag>-<chunk_n> scheme makes one repo a striped volume of unlimited size.
limits_note: Pull count 100/6h anonymous or 200/6h authenticated per IP — that is the binding constraint for a 500GB-1TiB/day fetch workload (needs few, large blobs rather than many small ones). No published per-layer size cap, but the Docker distribution S3 driver historically broke above 10GB per layer (distribution/distribution#2814), so shard at ~5GB. The excess-use rate limit returns plain 429 in the order of thousands of req/min per IP.

identity_cost.detail: derived from the record's prose, not from an identity field, and no signup was executed: repo a striped volume of unlimited size.
